problem:
Let $V={R}_{1}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $1,$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(-1)y(-1)+x(1)y(1).
$$

If $p(t)=2t+4$ and $q(t)=kt+2$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
worked_solution:
Since $p(t)$ and $q(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(-1)q(-1)+p(1)q(1) \\  & =(2)(-k+2)+(6)(k+2) \\  & =-2k+4+6k+12 \\  & =4k+16\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =0 \\ 4k+16 & =0 \\ 4k & =-16 \\ k & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
